- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.40) — model fails to capture sharp downside moves.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays mean reversion, especially after strong spikes — adjust forecast downward 1–2 periods after peak sentiment.
- Overshoot after sentiment reversal: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model continues upward — reduce forecast by 5–15% in next 3–5 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows — apply smoothing filter or decay weights to recent history (e.g., 70% weight on 14-day avg).
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — dampen forecast volatility for longer horizons (e.g., reduce std dev by 30% if sentiment volatility > 0.30).
